description:
Spotted during JMAP-sc1b.109 chat-server AGENTS.md spot-check (2026-05-12).

The chat-server AGENTS.md added a 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section (lines 74-97 in crate-jmap-chat-server/AGENTS.md as of 2026-05-12) that documents:
  - Backends are canonical for permission enforcement (per workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' rule)
  - Handlers do NO permission checking; defense-in-depth handler-side pre-checks allowed but backend MUST re-verify atomically
  - Caller identity via JmapBackend::principal_id; None-returning backends cannot honor identity-dependent JMAP semantics
  - Extension-specific implications (chat-server's version calls out Space mutations and the implementation-defined ownership posture from JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12)

This is **workspace-wide policy**, not chat-specific content. The canonical jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md (109 lines) does not currently carry this section. Per the workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' propagation rule, additions made on a sibling should backport to the canonical so future cookie-cuts produce complete files.

## Acceptance

  - crate-jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md grows a 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section with:
    - Workspace-wide policy paragraph (verbatim from chat-server's lines 74-89)
    - Mail-specific implications paragraph replacing chat-server's lines 90-97. Likely content: per-user $seen on shared mailboxes (RFC 8621 §4.1.1), Identity/EmailSubmission authorization, mailbox role-based access where applicable.
  - The section lives in the same position as chat-server's (after 'Reference Pattern', before 'Non-Interactive Shell Commands').
  - Sweep follow-up: once the 6-sibling sweep from JMAP-sc1b.109 lands (chat-server cookie-cut into calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing/metadata), each of those 6 files also needs its own extension-specific implications paragraph in place of the chat-specific one. File this as part of the same sweep work or as a follow-up nit.

## Out of scope

  - Reshaping the section content itself (the chat-server wording is the authoritative shape; this is just a backport + per-extension swap of the trailing implications paragraph).
  - Adding any workspace-wide policy that isn't already in chat-server's section.

## Cross-references

  - JMAP-sc1b.109 — the spot-check that surfaced this gap (chat-server's new section)
  - JMAP-ga0q — the foundation-seam work that authorizes 'backends are canonical for permission enforcement'
  - workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' — the policy this section operationalizes per-crate
title: Backport 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section to canonical jmap-mail-server/AGENTS.md
